text:
Aliaksei Protas has been bounced around Washington's lineup this season, and the numbers suggest he deserves a steadier spot. Tom Gulitti of NHL.com reported the Capitals moved him out of the middle in last week's shuffle, and he answered with a goal and an assist in Saturday's 4-3 win over Florida.

He has seven points in 15 games, below the pace of his 52-point season a year ago, mostly because the finishing is light: two goals on 2.8 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 10.5% against a typical 12 to 16%. Washington has 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, so the play is fine.

He's a third-round pick from Belarus who grew into a top-six forward. Evolving-Hockey had him driving offense last season (92nd percentile among forwards) while giving some back defensively (bottom 10%), which is the trade with him. Our projection has him around 19 goals. Wherever the Capitals put him, we'd expect more scoring than he's shown so far.
